newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr soars on rate hopes, Eurobourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr soars on rate hopes, Eurobourses mixed.

text.p: The dollar surged on Monday, climbing to a four-year high against the Swiss franc, an eight-year peak against the French franc and mark and nearly a 12-year high against the lira on expectations U.S interest rates will soon rise.

Interest rate jitters forced the Dow Jones Industrial Average to drop sharply in early trade and weigh on most European bourses in the afternoon. But Finnish shares were the exception, eking out a record high after impressive earnings results from Nokia Ab, Oy's.
The dollar jumped on speculation the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates at its next policy-making meeting on August 19 to curb strong growth and keep inflation in check.

U.S. July nonfarm payrolls rose 316,000 and the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) July prices paid index rose above 50 for the first time in four months on Friday. A NAPM index above 50 usually points to expansion, while a figure below 50 indicates contraction.
That, coupled with perceptions Germany's economy remained too fragile to bear an imminent rate rise, kept the dollar climbing throughout the day.
Originally, traders were speculating on a German rate rise via the central bank's weekly money market operation.

Before leaving for its four-week summer recess, the Bundesbank set its weekly money market operations at a fixed 3.0 percent for two weeks. Traders speculated the Bundesbank was leaving room for rates to drift higher in the last two holiday weeks by setting a variable rate tender.

Talk even circulated that the German central bank would not wait two weeks before setting a variable rate tender. Instead, it could set a second money market operation this week in addition to its fixed-rate tender depending on key German jobless data due on Wednesday.

But most traders have since dismissed such talk, and the dollar rose until some investors sold to lock in profits made in the latest leg up. That selling knocked the dollar off its peak in late European trading.
Though the dollar benefitted from interest rate speculation, stocks did not fare as well.
Uncertainty about Bundesbank policy rattled Germany's blue-chip DAX index. The DAX ended bourse trade down 111.85 points, or more than 2.50 percent, at 4,296.94.

Bank shares led the declines. Commerzbank AG ended down 1.15 marks at 61.50, Deutsche Bank AG down 4.75 at 117.40, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG down 3.90 at 72.05 and Bay Vereinsbank was down 3.00 at 95.80.
London's FTSE-100 index extended losses after the Dow opened weak and quickly extended losses to set off the New York Stock Exchange's trading curbs.
But FTSE cut its losses were cut after the Dow recouped some of its decline.
London's drop was also tempered by HSBC Holdings Plc 's jump to a year high of 2,326 pence on better-than-expected first-half results.

The bank said pre-tax profits in sterling terms rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds ($4.3 billion), with dividends up 33 percent to 20 pence per share. That compares with analysts' forecasts for pre-tax profits between 2.32 and 2.48 billion pounds.
FTSE activity was limited with British interest rate worries looming. The Bank of England's monetary policy-setting meeting is on Wednesday and Thursday.
A Reuters poll taken on July 30 showed 16 of 23 economists expected official British interest rates to rise 25 basis points after the meeting for the fourth rate rise in so many months.
French shares also slumped to end down nearly two percent below 3,000 as Wall Street tumbled. But volume was below average because many French traders were on holiday.
Finland's FOX index was an exception, scoring a record high after Nokia's first-half earnings report.
The mobile phone maker said first-half profits of 3.33 billion markka ($5.9 billion) to beat a Reuters survey of expectations for 3.09 billion and the highest forecast in the survey of 3.3 billion.
Nokia shares closed up 5.50 markka at 478.00, off its year high of 485 markka made in early trade. The FOX index ended up 3.40 at 1,241.58, just off its record 1,244.41.
The blue-chip Dutch AEX index erased early gains to end down 1.39 points at 979.35 as New York shares fell and traders searched for the next market trend.
"There's some fear in the market. People are no longer that convinced (of the uptrend). They're looking for a direction," a dealer said.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.8635 marks and 118.40 yen compared to 1.8630 and 118.37 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished down 3.6 points at 4,895.70.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trade down 111.85 points at 4,296.94. The DAX IBIS index fell 34.48 points to 4,302.50 in electronic trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 57.03 points at 2,992.41.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended in London at $323.65, down from Friday's close at $324.25.
($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
($ = 5.552 Finnish Markka)
